candidate.title: Nextera Library Preparation
candidate.scope: The unversioned Nextera Library Preparation component schematic: DNA engagement by transposase, tagmentation, an index-bearing primer intermediate, and amplification to a product ready for cluster generation. The title identifies one target workflow and depicts no alternative. The substrate is DNA; its biological source and any upstream RNA-to-DNA conversion are not specified. The approximately 300 bp annotation describes the pictured fragment rather than a universal Nextera size requirement. Cluster generation and sequencing are downstream interfaces, not depicted operations.

states.label: DNA substrate
features: Two parallel blue lines depict double-stranded DNA.
No specimen, biological locus, or upstream preparation is identified.

evidence.locator: Upper substrate row labelled DNA, below the free Transposase icons

states.label: DNA engaged by transposase complexes
features: The blue double-stranded DNA remains continuous in this row.
Two blue transposase icons contact the DNA with magenta and green tag-like elements; these colours are retained in the later DNA end regions.

evidence.locator: Second DNA row, with two transposase icons on the DNA

states.label: Tagmented DNA fragments with coloured end tags
features: The previously continuous DNA is interrupted at the magenta and green regions, depicting fragmentation with tagging.
A central double-stranded DNA segment is flanked by a magenta end region on the left and a green end region on the right, with approximately 300 bp indicated above it.
Shorter flanking DNA portions are also drawn. The next arrow follows a representative central fragment; no separate branch processing or fragment-selection operation is shown.

evidence.locator: Fragment row beneath Tagmentation, including the ~300bp label and flanking DNA portions

states.label: Tagged DNA insert with index-bearing amplification oligonucleotides
features: The blue DNA insert is drawn between magenta and green terminal regions.
An outward extension at the left is labelled P5 and Index 2; the opposite outward extension is labelled Index 1 and P7.
The extensions are drawn at opposite ends and on opposite sides of the duplex, preserving their association with the tagged insert.

evidence.locator: Intermediate below the fragment row: left P5/Index 2 arm and right Index 1/P7 arm

states.label: Amplified indexed DNA library ready for cluster generation
features: The final linear product retains the blue insert between coloured terminal sequences.
The final row places P5 and Index 2 to the left of the blue insert and Index 1 and P7 to its right; the coloured terminal segments are schematic and exact nucleotide sequences are not given.
The final row is a single-line schematic and does not establish the strand count of the finished library.
The source explicitly labels this product ready for cluster generation.

evidence.locator: Bottom product row labelled P5, Index 2, Index 1 and P7, beside Product ready for cluster generation

operations.label: Transposase engagement of DNA (unlabelled arrow)
operations.description: The continuous DNA substrate becomes associated with two depicted transposase complexes. The enzyme icons are reagents acting on the DNA, rather than independent biological sample branches.
operations.mechanism: The top row labels the blue protein icons Transposase and shows magenta or green elements beneath them; the downward arrow leads to the same icons contacting the DNA. No enzyme subtype or detailed binding chemistry is specified.
operations.information_effect: The substrate remains continuous in the engagement intermediate; no index-labelled sequence has yet been depicted on the DNA.

evidence.locator: Top Transposase/DNA row, first downward arrow, and enzyme-engaged DNA row

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: The transposase-engaged continuous DNA becomes fragmented DNA with magenta and green tag regions at the illustrated break sites. The central tagged segment, marked approximately 300 bp, is the representative fragment carried into the next drawing.
operations.mechanism: The Transposase-labelled complexes and the Tagmentation arrow support transposase-mediated fragmentation and tagging as a coupled schematic transformation; exact end chemistry and tag sequences are not resolved.
operations.information_effect: Input-derived blue DNA sequence is retained in shorter inserts, with coloured terminal tags providing the depicted connection to subsequent amplification oligonucleotides. The original continuous DNA molecule is no longer represented as intact.

evidence.locator: Enzyme-engaged DNA, downward arrow labelled Tagmentation, and tagged fragment row

operations.label: Association of index-bearing amplification oligonucleotides (unlabelled arrow)
operations.description: The representative tagged DNA fragment is next drawn with terminal oligonucleotide extensions carrying P5/Index 2 on the left and Index 1/P7 on the right. This records the depicted primer-bearing intermediate without adding an unshown ligation or end-repair operation.
operations.information_effect: Index-labelled and P5/P7-labelled sequences become associated with the insert at opposite ends in the amplification intermediate. The diagram gives no mapping of either index to a biological specimen or unit.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from the ~300bp fragment row to the P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 arm intermediate
Terminal arms in the intermediate immediately above Amplification
evidence.rationale: Interpreting the arms as amplification oligonucleotides follows from their contact with opposite tagged ends, their outward index/P5/P7 extensions, and the next labelled operation Amplification. The drawing does not resolve the detailed annealing or extension chemistry.

operations.label: Amplification
operations.description: The primer-bearing tagged DNA intermediate is amplified into the final insert-containing library with both index regions and the P5/P7 terminal regions represented in the product.
operations.mechanism: Amplification is explicitly labelled; enzymes, cycles and any internal completion steps are not specified.
operations.information_effect: The physical readout carrier is the resulting DNA library molecule: its blue insert represents a fragment of input DNA, and the same molecule carries the two index-labelled regions. Sequencing this library could interrogate the retained DNA insert, but neither sequence data nor a biological expression measurement is depicted. The P5/P7-ended product is shown as an input suitable for subsequent cluster generation.

evidence.locator: Final downward arrow labelled Amplification, leading from the primer-bearing intermediate to Product ready for cluster generation
Blue insert retained through the DNA, fragment, intermediate and final product rows
evidence.rationale: The arrows and repeated blue insert connect the initial DNA substrate to the final DNA library. Thus a downstream sequence readout would concern retained input-DNA sequence; the diagram supplies no upstream biological identity or RNA conversion that would establish a more specific biological measurement.

method_scopes.rationale: The card and figure have the same single method title. All four successive depicted transitions belong to this product-preparation schematic; there are no alternative methods or retained independent processing branches. This resolves applicability for the assigned unversioned depiction, not for every Nextera product implementation. No primary-paper association is required or supplied, so architecture support comes from the diagram and title rather than a publication claim.

Title Nextera Library Preparation and complete downward workflow

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the candidate's single-workflow architecture: continuous DNA, enzyme-associated DNA, tagged fragments, a two-ended index-bearing intermediate, and amplified library. All four arrows are represented. The flanking fragment portions are acknowledged without inventing separate processing or size selection. The blue insert supplies the input-DNA representation in the final physical readout carrier; the source specifies neither biological specimen nor an upstream RNA conversion. Index and P5/P7 associations are retained, and no compartment, attachment, alternative workflow, or depicted branch is omitted. The supplied card has no references and explicitly does not require a paper match; empty paper_matches and corrections are appropriate. No consequential claim depends on unavailable primary-paper chemistry, and no blocking unknown remains within this schematic scope.
